claims.text: A Pt-based high-entropy alloy containing several secondary elements will have greater intrinsic HER/HOR activity than conventional Pt catalysts.
The proposed Pt-based high-entropy alloy will have superior long-term durability to conventional Pt catalysts.
Traditional Pt-based catalysts have high catalytic activity.
Traditional Pt-based catalysts suffer degradation and Pt dissolution under electrochemical conditions.
The proposed catalyst can be synthesized by combining Pt with secondary elements such as Ni, Co, Ru, and Mo in near-equiatomic or optimized ratios.
The intended operating domain includes acidic or alkaline HER/HOR environments at ambient to moderate temperatures.
The proposed multi-element composition will form a stabilized solid-solution structure.
The multi-element composition will tailor the catalyst's surface electronic properties.
The high-entropy composition will resist corrosive oxidation and dissolution.
Alloying Pt with additional elements alters its electronic structure.
The altered electronic structure modifies the adsorption energies of hydrogen intermediates.
Alloying Pt with the proposed secondary elements increases phase stability.
Modified hydrogen adsorption and increased phase stability reduce catalyst degradation.
Modified hydrogen adsorption and increased phase stability improve HER/HOR kinetics.
The proposed catalyst will deliver an approximately 10–20% activity gain relative to conventional Pt.
The proposed catalyst will degrade more slowly during extended electrochemical cycling than conventional Pt.
Excessive dilution of Pt active sites could negate the proposed performance improvement.
Unfavorable phase segregation could negate the proposed performance improvement.
The catalyst's performance may vary with electrolyte pH and operating temperature.
The precise elemental ratios and processing conditions needed to balance activity and durability remain undetermined.
